intro: Expo pavilions at conferences are temporary, custom-built structures used by organizations, companies, or countries to showcase products, services, innovations, and cultural identity. They are a key part of large international exhibitions and conferences, designed to create a unique, engaging, and memorable experience for visitors. These pavilions can range from individual company booths to large, elaborate national buildings that are later dismantled or repurposed after the event ends.
highlights: Exhibitors are the creators and experts who showcase new tools, tests and ideas.
Make a list of your must-see brands so you don’t miss what matters most.
Prepare questions for exhibitors to turn short chats into real insights.
Explore small emerging brands too, as they often bring bold and fresh solutions.
Respect booth staff by waiting your turn and giving each demo the space it needs.

blocks.text: What Is an Expo at a Biohacking Conference?

The exhibition pavilions at the Biohacking conference, where events are held, offer exhibitors modern engineering and technical capabilities and feature spacious, multifunctional halls for seminars, conferences, and meetings. The large areas allow you to showcase products and services of any size or complexity, hold tastings, PR events, and negotiations, conduct surveys, and distribute samples or business souvenirs. Everything that could interest any biohacker, expert, or athlete!

Here you have a unique opportunity to be the first to learn about all the latest products, innovations, and technical developments from companies, or to get early access to unique courses or programs. Exclusivity, authenticity, and a narrow audience are what distinguish expo from any other format.

Types of Exhibitors You’ll Find

Get ready to dive into the world of possibility at the upcoming Biohacking Conference & Expo. Whether you’re a curious attendee, a serious networker, or someone hunting down the next big wellness breakthrough, the expo zone is your discovery pass. The expo area features many partners of the event organizers. Here you can buy products, try out the latest developments, and meet the creators.
Product Showcases

These are the eye-catching, tech-driven corners of the expo — where innovation meets design. You’ll find everything from sleek wearable devices and smart recovery tools to next-generation biofeedback systems. Stop here to get hands-on with the technology, see how it works in real life, and talk to the minds behind the products. They’re usually happy to walk you through their latest upgrade or reveal what’s coming next. It’s a chance to see the future of personal optimization — up close.
Interactive Demo Booths

This is where the energy spikes. These booths invite you to experience the science firsthand — through immersive VR setups, neurostimulation demos, or cutting-edge recovery systems. Don’t just observe — participate. Feel how your body or mind responds, notice what changes, and use the opportunity to engage directly with the creators. Their passion often says as much about the innovation as the technology itself.
On-site Diagnostics and Assessments

Some exhibitors bring science right to the floor. From metabolic scans and body-composition testing to DNA or epigenetic profiling, these booths offer personalized data in real time. It’s one thing to read about optimization — it’s another to see your own biomarkers light up on a screen. If you stop by, be curious. Ask what the results mean for your daily life and how you can apply them beyond the conference.
Supplement and Nutraceutical Brands

Expect an abundance of capsules, powders, and tonics — all promising to elevate your health. But this isn’t just a supplement marketplace; it’s an education hub. Many founders and formulators are on site, ready to talk about their sourcing, research, and testing. It’s a great opportunity to understand how science, ethics, and entrepreneurship intersect in the world of nutraceuticals. And yes, you’ll probably walk away with a few samples — and a few new insights.

Wellness & Therapy Experience Zones

Beyond the gadgets and formulas, you’ll find zones designed for immersion — sensory spaces where you can test different recovery or relaxation modalities. Maybe you’ll try red-light therapy, guided breathwork, or a restorative pod that feels like floating in another dimension. These experiences are not just for rest; they showcase what daily wellness could look like when technology supports mindfulness and balance. Take a few moments to simply be present — and see how your body reacts.
How to Get the Most Out of Exhibitors
Expo exhibitors offer many opportunities and prizes to all conference participants during the expo. Take your time while you are there!
Check the List of Exhibitors in Advance

Plan in advance to attend lectures and visit exhibition at conference. Don’t forget to check the agenda and read about the speakers and companies. Conferences may also send out newsletters — subscribe to them, as they may contain additional information and materials from partners.
Select Your Must-See Companies

First, make a list of the companies that interest you most so you can learn about their products and future plans. Start by visiting them first — that way, you won’t miss anything important that interests you. Interest and necessity come first!
Research Companies and Prepare Questions

Of course, prepare for communication with company representatives. Learn more about their strategy, goals, and plans, priority areas of work, prominent representatives and ambassadors, and study their financial position and reputation. You may have questions or suggestions — then the event will be a unique opportunity to discuss them in person. The main thing is not to miss opportunities.

[Networking](https://www.biohackers.world/blog/how-to-network-at-biohacking-conferences) at specialized conferences rarely brings you into contact with strangers. Therefore, try to start as many conversations as possible during your visit. Such activity is analogous to a long-term investment in your own social capital.
Take Notes or Record Key Insights

It is almost impossible to remember everything the speaker says, and recording with a smartphone is sometimes prohibited by the event’s rules. Most often, people use good old notebooks — you can take notes with key points, announcements of events or releases, names of specialists, or product names. If you can’t use a laptop, smartphone, or voice recorder, a pen and notebook are a good alternative. First, you won’t bother others with the light from your devices. Second, writing by hand is the best way to remember information because it engages multiple memory systems at once.
Look for Giveaways and Free Samples

The golden rule of conferences: if they give it to you, take it! Don’t miss the chance to try something new at such events — as a rule, you will be one of the first to test something or learn more about upcoming releases or market innovations.

Handouts, gifts, samples, and trial sizes are all provided to conference participants for their convenience and to increase brand awareness. And why not try your luck in contests? It’s a superb chance to show off your skills and get some lovely gifts from brands!

What NOT to Do at a Biohacking Conference
Even the most curious biohacker can miss out if they approach the conference expo floor the wrong way. To make your experience truly valuable — and leave a great impression — here’s what to avoid.

items: **Don’t show up unprepared.** Wandering aimlessly from booth to booth rarely leads to meaningful insights. Take a few minutes to research the expo exhibitors you’re most interested in. Having a short list of “must-visit” stands and a few smart questions makes all the difference.

**Don’t collect samples chaotically.** Yes, the freebies are tempting — but quality and necessity beat quantity. Focus on products that genuinely interest you, ask how to use them properly, and note any contraindications. Your body (and your suitcase) will thank you later.

**Don’t be pushy.** Exhibitors are there to engage — but respect their time and space. If a booth is crowded, wait for your turn. If a rep looks busy with a demo, come back in a few minutes. Authentic curiosity always makes a better impression than forced enthusiasm.

**Don’t ignore the rules and instructions.** Every setup — especially diagnostic or interactive ones — comes with its own safety and usage guidelines. Follow them carefully. This ensures both your comfort and the accuracy of any results or data you receive.

**Don’t forget to network.** Business cards and LinkedIn scans are fine, but real connections come from conversation. Ask thoughtful questions, share your own experiences, and thank people for their time — you never know what collaboration might grow from it. The main rule is simple: just attending the conference is not enough. You need to meet people, gain new knowledge, and exchange experiences.

**Don’t rush through everything.** The conference expo floor is a sensory overload of lights, data, and ideas. Slow down. Take breaks. Integrate what you learn. Sometimes the best insights come not from more information, but from giving your brain a moment to process.

blocks.text: Quick Tips from Experienced Attendees
Want to navigate the Biohacking Conference & Expo like a pro? These insider moves will help you make the most of your time — and maybe even score some unexpected perks.

items: **Join expo giveaways and scan those QR codes.**

blocks.text: Almost every booth has some kind of digital raffle or bonus for attendees. A quick scan can lead to exclusive discounts, early access to new releases, or even free testing sessions.

Take photos in the themed zones, share your favorite finds, tag sponsors, and use event hashtags. Not only does it spread the energy, it often gets noticed by expo exhibitors, who may reward the engagement with extra samples or VIP invites.
Crowds are thinnest early in the morning or near closing time — perfect moments to have meaningful one-on-one conversations without the rush.
Don’t overlook the new players. Startups often bring their most innovative ideas and are eager to build relationships — plus, their samples and gifts tend to be surprisingly generous.

items: **Talk to the founders when you can.**

blocks.text: Many expo exhibitors are the creators themselves — the scientists, engineers, or visionaries behind the product. Speaking directly with them can give you insights you won’t find in any brochure.

With so many findings in one place, details blur fast. Put down your favorite finds, brands to revisit, or questions that sparked your curiosity — it’ll make your post-event follow-up much more productive.
To sum up

Visiting the conference expo zone at Biohacking Conference & Expo is an excellent opportunity to gain not only theoretical knowledge and listen to speakers, but also be the first to touch the latest technologies and scientific developments, and try new biohacking brand products in one place. With our tips, we are sure it will be easy for you! Have fun and see you at the nearest event!
